title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2611.32138v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene content from clips with low initial anomaly scores and uses this estimate to partially correct the textual reference. translated_title: VIDE：基于视觉内在分布估计的无训练视频异常检测
translated_abstract: 在基于嵌入的视频异常检测（VAD）中，正常片段可能与异常描述具有高相似度，这种异常偏差会导致误报。诸如PRISM等方法通过测量沿异常方向相对于正常性参考的偏差来缓解这一问题。然而，正常性参考和异常方向均从文本中导出，并在所有视频之间共享，尽管正常活动和异常的表现形式在不同场景中各不相同。由此产生的评分对提示词的选择也十分敏感。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了视觉内在分布估计（VIDE），这是一个无需训练的框架，它利用冻结的片段嵌入将基于文本的评分适配到每个测试视频中。VIDE从初始异常分数较低的片段中估计正常场景内容，并利用该估计对文本参考进行部分修正。随后，它重新调整类别响应的尺度，并对在多个类别上具有强烈响应的片段进行惩罚。
tldr: VIDE是一种无需训练的视频异常检测框架，通过利用冻结片段嵌入估计每个测试视频的正常场景内容分布，自适应修正文本参考并重调整类别响应，从而减少跨场景误报并降低对提示词选择的敏感性。
en_tdlr: VIDE is a training-free video anomaly detection framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video by estimating normal scene content from frozen clip embeddings, correcting the textual reference and rescaling category responses to reduce false positives and prompt sensitivity.
